title: Motion graphs and reproducible data work
rows: x: position from a stated origin; chosen positive direction; unit m. Δx = x₂ − x₁. A position is not a distance travelled.
Δt = t₂ − t₁ > 0; unit s. Clock reading and elapsed time differ.
Average velocity = displacement / elapsed time. Average speed = total distance / elapsed time. Include stops in the interval. Units m/s.
x_pred(t) = x_ref + v(t − t_ref). One fixed coordinate system; v constant over the modelled interval.
r = x_observed − x_predicted, at the same time; unit m. Positive: observed position lies on positive side of prediction.
Position–time gradient gives interval average velocity between endpoints. A straight model segment asserts constant velocity; isolated points do not.
Endpoints give net displacement. Total distance needs the path; equal endpoint positions need not mean rest.
Interpolation: inside stated data interval. Extrapolation: outside it. Neither guarantees accuracy. Construction-point agreement is built in.
Unchanged identified source + units/origin/clock + selection rule + declared model + saved code + labelled output + actual fresh-run/version note.
Hand prediction/residual; reference-time and zero-velocity checks; fresh ordered run. Missing is not zero. Code execution is not physical validation.
python:
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
p = Path.cwd() / "data" / "record.csv"
a = np.genfromtxt(p, delimiter=",", skip_header=1,
    dtype=float, filling_values=np.nan,
    ndmin=2, loose=False)
print(a.shape)  # inspect expected rows and columns

t_all = a[:, 0]
x_all = a[:, 1]
keep = np.isfinite(t_all) & np.isfinite(x_all)
t = t_all[keep]
x = x_all[keep]
print(t_all[~keep])  # omitted times; source unchanged

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(t, x, "o", label="Available observations")
ax.set_xlabel("Clock reading / s")
ax.set_ylabel("Position / m")
ax.legend()
fig.savefig("positions.png", dpi=160)
plt.show()

import platform
import matplotlib
print(platform.python_version())
print(np.__version__, matplotlib.__version__)
